title: Toggle Visibility
description:
Create a component that toggles the visibility of content when a button is clicked. This exercise teaches conditional rendering in React - one of the most fundamental concepts for building interactive UIs.

For example:
- Initially, no message is visible
- After clicking 'Toggle': 'Hello, I am visible!' appears
- After clicking 'Toggle' again: the message disappears

You'll use boolean state (true/false) instead of numbers, and learn the && operator for conditional rendering.
requirements: Use React.useState hook to manage a boolean 'isVisible' state (starting as false)
Render a button with text 'Toggle' that changes the state when clicked
When isVisible is true, display a paragraph with the text 'Hello, I am visible!'
When isVisible is false, the paragraph should not be rendered at all
Export the ToggleVisibility component as the default export
hints: Use boolean state: const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(false)
Toggle the value: setIsVisible(!isVisible) or setIsVisible(prev => !prev)

Use conditional rendering with &&: {isVisible &&

Hello, I am visible!

}
The && operator means: if left side is true, render right side
